title: Cops cleared in fatal shooting
article: The province's civilian police watchdog has cleared two York Regional Police officers who fatally shot a Thornhill man suspected of stabbing his wife to death.

York police were called to 90 Cottonwood Crt., in the Leslie and John streets area of Markham, Aug. 1 after the force received a 911 call about blood in the home, the Special Investigations Unit said today.
Eight officers arrived at the home - some went in through the front door and others through a sliding door at the back of the home.
In the kitchen, police found Nasrin Toreihi, 47, unconscious on the floor. Her body had been stabbed several times, the SIU said.
Her estranged spouse, Kaveh Sabouri Tabatabaei, 50, was lying beside her with his left hand holding her right hand and his right hand holding a large kitchen knife.
As Mr. Tabatabaei alternated between stabbing himself and swinging the knife at police, the officers drew their guns and yelled at him to drop the blade, the SIU said.

Police made several attempts to subdue Mr. Tabatabaei, including pinning him with a chair, using pepper spray and an expandable baton, but were unsuccessful because he continued to lunge with the knife.
None of the officers at the scene had been assigned a Taser.
Two of the officers decided they needed to shoot Mr. Tabatabaei and fired, the SIU said.
Mr. Tabatabaei and Ms Toreihi died at the scene.

The officers were justified in entering the home without a warrant due to the exceptional circumstances involved in the incident and in using lethal force against Mr. Tabatabaei to keep him from further injuring Ms Toreihi, SIU Director Ian Scott said.
